# Intake Brief — Reduce per-invocation cost of the transient `wl` processes (WL-0MVFNMSRW002FI6B)

## Problem statement (headline)

Every `wl` command spawns a fresh Node.js process that takes **0.6–1.7 s and 80–180 MB** just to boot (a bare `node -e ''` is 0.35 s / 58 MB): the CLI eagerly imports 40+ modules (commander, all ~35 command builders, plugins, runtime, `better-sqlite3`) before any command logic, and herdr panes + pi agents fire these one-shot processes continuously (30 s refresh ticks, 60 s `sync --if-idle` per pane, per-agent polls). Four concurrent `wl` processes were observed at 25–65 % CPU each — bursty, seconds-long, gone moments later. The shipped read-cache (WL-0MSAZQEQB008O7H3) cut *read work* (83 %) but deliberately left process spawning unchanged ("each invocation still spawns a wl process"). There is also an unbounded hygiene leak: `~/.cache/wl/state/` holds **216,228 one-file-per-worklog-dir counters (~890 MB, 216k inodes)** that are never pruned.

## Users

- **Herdr TUI panes / pi agents** — the heaviest spawners; every 30–60 s tick pays full process boot even for cache hits.
  - *As a herdr pane, I want cache-hit refreshes to cost near bare-node boot, so refresh cycles stop stealing core-seconds from the host.*
- **Operators / agents running ad-hoc `wl` commands** — every `wl create/update/comment/sync/next` pays the same boot cost.
  - *As an operator, I want `wl` commands to feel instant, so interactive and agent-driven use stops producing CPU bursts.*
- **Host administrators** — transient process bursts and an unbounded 890 MB cache dir degrade a shared Raspberry Pi / herdr server.
  - *As an admin, I want spawn load and cache disk bounded, so the host stays responsive.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- **(AC1)** **Import budget on the fast path:** the cache-hit read path and `--version` must not load command modules, the DB runtime, or plugins. Measured on the reference host (this repo, node ≥ 20): p95 wall time for a warm repeated `wl next --json` / `list --status open --json` cache hit ≤ **0.5 s** and peak RSS ≤ **60 MB** (current: ~0.6–1.2 s / 80–160 MB; bare node 0.35 s / 58 MB — the margin is deliberately tiny, so the fast-path import set must be slimmer than today's `read-cache-cli` graph at 61 MB). Enforced by a regression benchmark/test (e.g. asserts the heavy modules are not imported on the fast path).
- **(AC2)** **Measurable spawn-load reduction:** total CPU-seconds per 30 s refresh cycle across ≥ 4 panes on one shared worklog dir drops **≥ 60 %** versus current behaviour, measured by extending the env-gated spawn instrumentation (`WL_SPAWN_COUNT_FILE`, src/spawn-counter.ts) to record per-process CPU time (`process.resourceUsage().user+system`); baseline and after numbers quoted in the work item.
- **(AC3)** **Cache hygiene / bounded on-disk state:** `~/.cache/wl/state/` (216,228 files, ~890 MB, one file per worklog dir ever seen) is bounded and prunable — after a run, state storage is capped (bounded file count, or consolidated storage) and stale entries are removed; a documented maintenance path (`wl doctor cache` or automatic pruning) reclaims it. Freshness semantics unchanged (no correctness regression).
- **(AC4)** **No correctness regression:** all read-cache invariants from WL-0MSAZQEQB008O7H3 hold — write→read freshness, arg-variant separation, WAL-aware invalidation, concurrent readers/writers, byte-identical JSON for identical (dir, argv, version). The existing read-cache/e2e/spawn-reduction suites pass unchanged.
- **(AC5)** **Graceful degradation:** if lazy loading or the split entry point fails for any command, behaviour falls back to today's fully-registered CLI (no functional regression, help/plugin registration intact).
- **(AC6)** **Tests + docs:** unit/integration/benchmark tests cover the fast path, lazy loading, CPU-time instrumentation and cache hygiene; related documentation (CLI.md / CONFIG.md / docs as appropriate) updated; full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- **Stateless one-shot CLI** — no daemon, no long-lived server, no IPC worker (operator decision, Q1-A). Architecture and on-disk Git/JSONL sync semantics must not change.
- `wl` must keep working from any worktree/`--worklog-dir` (the prefix-to-sibling resolution and worklog-dir override must not be disturbed by splitting the entry point).
- Cache correctness invariants (WAL aware, TTL 30 s, LRU bound) are **non-negotiable** — the fast path only shortens import time.
- Node ESM, build via `tsc` to `dist/`; `/usr/local/bin/wl` symlinks into this repo's `dist/cli.js` (v1.0.22) — keep that contract intact.
- Performance benchmarks must be CPU-time based / tolerant on shared hosts (a Raspberry Pi, herdr server).

## Existing state

- Read-cache epic **shipped (WL-0MSAZQEQB008O7H3, v1.0.9)**: identical JSON reads (list/next/show/search/status) served pre-parse from `~/.cache/wl` with 83 % read-work reduction, sync+heartbeat, herdr in-process memoisation. Its audit records the accepted variance: "each invocation still spawns a wl process that exits without DB work" — the spawn itself was left in scope.
- pi-extension poll gating shipped (WL-0MSB1N0HB0007N6N + tests WL-0MSB446N4009FFT5); orphaned worktree process lifecycle shipped (WL-0MRP1SLZB005ZNYO).
- Herdr cadence: 30 s refresh × 4–5 wl fetches per pane, 60 s auto-sync with 45 s cross-instance heartbeat (packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts).
- Measured here: `node -e ''` 0.35 s/58 MB; `wl --version` 0.95 s/80 MB; `wl list --json` (repeated) 0.6–1.2 s/80–160 MB; `wl status` 1.74 s/180 MB; `wl sync --if-idle` 1.39 s/116 MB; importing `dist/cli-utils.js` alone 0.60 s/73 MB; `dist/read-cache-cli.js` 0.46 s/61 MB.

## Desired change

1. **Split the entry point:** keep `src/cli.ts` thin — argv scan + read-cache fast path (imports only `read-cache-cli`, `spawn-counter`, `worklog-paths` + minimal utils), then **dynamically import** the current heavy graph (`./cli-main.ts` or lazy command map). Cache hits and `--version` exit before commander/DB/plugins load.
2. **Lazy per-command imports:** replace the 35 eager `import XCommand` lines with a registry resolving each command on demand; `--help` / bare invocation may load all (rare).
3. **Extend spawn instrumentation** with per-process CPU time (ru_utime/ru_stime) to measure CPU-second reduction, not just spawn count.
4. **Cache hygiene:** bound/prune `~/.cache/wl/state/` (e.g. LRU/TTL over counter files, consolidate counters, housekeeping in `wl doctor`); optionally tidy stale top-level entries.
5. **If ≥60 % CPU-second reduction is not reached by import slimming alone** (spawn count unchanged), coalesce repeated herdr reads into fewer wl invocations (still stateless, e.g. one batch query per refresh tick) — record which lever was needed.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/cli.ts` — split entry: 40 eager imports (lines ~6–47), cache fast path (~526–545) that currently runs only after the full graph loads.
- `src/read-cache-cli.ts` — cache lookup/backfill/invalidation orchestration; the fast-path import set.
- `src/read-cache.ts` — `state/` counter files (`stateCounterFilePath`/`bumpStateCounter`, ~157–200), purge/LRU, entry layout.
- `src/spawn-counter.ts` — extend `SpawnRecord` with CPU time.
- `src/commands/*.ts` — command modules to lazy-load (next, list, status, show, search, sync, …).
- `src/plugin-loader.ts`, `src/cli-utils.ts`, `src/lib/runtime.ts` — heavy imports to defer.
- `src/commands/doctor.ts` — cache maintenance command (state pruning).
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — coalescing repeated reads per refresh tick (only if needed to hit AC2).
- Tests: `tests/read-cache.test.ts`, `tests/read-cache-cli.test.ts`, `tests/cli/read-cache-e2e.test.ts`, `tests/cli/read-cache-spawn-reduction.test.ts`, new `tests/cli/startup-import-budget.test.ts` / CPU-time benchmark.

## Related work

- **WL-0MSB19J56006E87J (completed, v1.0.7) — "Investigate excessive wl process spawning (206 concurrent, ~17 GB RAM)"** — the predecessor investigation. It attacked spawn *count* (pi browse-widget idle-gating → WL-0MSB1N0HB0007N6N, herdr cadence, read-cache). **Not a duplicate:** it left per-invocation *cost* and on-disk cache hygiene untouched; this item targets boot cost + `state/` growth.
- WL-0MSAZQEQB008O7H3 (completed) — read-cache epic; the spawn cost was its accepted variance; this item continues from there.
- WL-0MSB1N0HB0007N6N / WL-0MSB446N4009FFT5 (completed) — visibility-gated polling in pi extension / herdr (spawn-count side).
- WL-0MRP1SLZB005ZNYO (completed) — orphaned node process lifecycle in worktrees.
- WL-0MRTSPLAX005Y8QY (completed) — process lifecycle documentation (reference for docs conventions).
- WL-0MULOZ37S007VV13 (completed) — metrics collection module (host metric collection precedent; candidate to reuse for CPU-second reporting).
- WL-0MUAD8U24001ZK5K (completed) — `wl sync` before refactor/standup skills (lock-aware `sync --if-idle` spawners).
- Duplicate check performed — no overlapping open/in-progress item targeting wl startup cost; `WL-0MSB19J56006E87J` covers the already-shipped spawn-count remediation only.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Lazy/help registration risk:** commander help and plugin registration must not regress — mitigated by AC5 fallback and deferring full registration to the heavy path.
- **Entry-point tests:** several suites import `src/cli.ts` / `dist/cli.js` directly; splitting must keep those contracts (tests/cli/cli-inproc.ts, inproc-harness, smoke, completion, …).
- **Benchmark flakiness** on shared hosts — AC1/AC2 measured by CPU time, p95 over repeated runs, generous margins above bare-node baseline.
- **State-dir pruning races:** pruning counters concurrently with writers must stay atomic (temp+rename, no regression of counter monotonicity).
- **Scope-creep guard:** daemon/server mode, JSONL/Git sync changes, and TUI redesign are explicitly out of scope — recorded as related opportunities, not work here.
- **Assumption:** the reference-host measurements above are representative of the failing hosts (same repo/worklog versions; herdr panes are the dominant spawner).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 — "What's the target shape of the improvement?" — Answer (rgardler): **A — keep `wl` a stateless one-shot CLI; lazy per-command imports, fast path for cache hits/`--version` at near-node-boot cost, plus cache hygiene (prune `state/`, bound growth). No daemon.** Source: interactive reply.
- Q2 — "How should we measure success?" — Answer (rgardler): **A — total CPU-seconds per refresh cycle ≥ 60 % reduction; per-process RSS < 60 MB; no correctness regression.** Source: interactive reply.
- Research summary: measured per-invocation cost (0.6–1.7 s / 80–180 MB vs 0.35 s / 58 MB bare node), attributed to eager 40-module import graph; verified the read-cache fast path still loads the full graph before serving (src/cli.ts); confirmed unbounded `~/.cache/wl/state/` (216,228 files / ~890 MB) with no pruning path.

## Related work (automated report)

Collected by `/skill:find-related` (sidecar: `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-WL-0MVFNMSRW002FI6B.md`).

### Related work items
- **WL-0MRTSPLAX005Y8QY** — Documentation for process lifecycle management (completed)
- **WL-0MULOZ37S007VV13** — Metrics collection module (completed)
- **WL-0MSB19J56006E87J** — Investigate excessive wl process spawning (206 concurrent, ~17 GB RAM) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — herdr cadence/spawner documentation
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — dispatcher/claim spawn context
- `CHANGELOG.md` — historical process-spawn/read-cache entries


---

## Plan — feature decomposition (plan skill, 2026-10-19)

Phasing is vertical slices (tracer bullets): measurement first, then the entry-point fast path, then cache hygiene, then the CPU-second verdict and docs. Each slice covers its own code, tests and docs; between phases, review the next items' descriptions and re-check the measured numbers.

| # | Child | Title | Type | Est. | Depends on | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | WL-0MVFRR98A008MM19 | Spawn instrumentation: per-process CPU and RSS | feature | S | — | Measure CPU-time and RSS per spawn (AC1 RSS, AC2) |
| F2 | WL-0MVFRRAXD001E7AN | Startup import-budget harness and baseline | feature | S | F1 | Ratchet + benchmark that lock in AC1 and capture the baseline |
| F3 | WL-0MVFRRCP7007UWS7 | Tests: thin entry-point split and dispatch parity | task | S | F2 | Test-first contracts for the entry split |
| F4 | WL-0MVFRRKKN00544PQ | Split CLI entry: thin fast path, dynamic heavy graph | feature | M | F3 | Fast path exits before commander/DB/plugins load (AC1) |
| F5 | WL-0MVFRREMZ0085G7I | Tests: lazy command registry, help and plugin fidelity | task | S | F4 | Test-first contracts incl. AC5 fallback |
| F6 | WL-0MVFRRMX3003UPP3 | Lazy per-command imports via command registry | feature | M | F5 | Load only the command that runs (AC1, AC5) |
| F7 | WL-0MVFRROLM002K98B | Fast-path import slimming to the 0.5 s / 60 MB budget | feature | M | F2, F4, F6 | Meet and freeze the AC1 numbers |
| F8 | WL-0MVFRRGGC001IQK1 | Tests: cache state pruning, bounds and atomicity | task | S | — | Test-first contracts for AC3 hygiene + AC4 freshness |
| F9 | WL-0MVFRRQ9W003KEFL | Bound and prune cache state via wl doctor cache | feature | M | F8 | Bounded `state/` store + documented maintenance path (AC3) |
| F10 | WL-0MVFRRS2I000G93J | Verify >=60% CPU-second reduction per refresh cycle | feature | M | F1, F6, F7 | AC2 measurement and herdr-coalescing verdict |
| F11 | WL-0MVFRRTY5001KTNH | Docs: fast path, instrumentation and cache maintenance | docs | XS | F1, F7, F9 | AC6 documentation half |

### Plan-stage decisions (recorded assumptions)

- **D1 — Budget enforcement is a ratchet, not a single hard-coded threshold.** AC1's 0.5 s / 60 MB budget is tighter than today's fast-path graph (0.46 s / 61 MB), so F2 checks in a budget file (`bench/startup-import-budget.json`) that records the statically reachable graph and the measured cost, and fails on growth. F4 and F7 tighten it in the change that improves it — keeping the suite green between items while locking in every improvement and making the regression test deterministic and host-load tolerant.
- **D2 — Peak RSS comes from the instrumented child.** `process.resourceUsage().maxRSS` is recorded per process by F1, so AC1's RSS check needs no external sampler.
- **D3 — Cache hygiene uses a bounded LRU plus TTL over `state/*.json`.** Consolidating counters into the cache entry files is only adopted if the bounded-file approach misses AC3's cap, because the counter atomicity and monotonicity invariant (`bumpStateCounter`) is the freshness guarantee and must not be rebuilt.
- **D4 — Herdr coalescing is conditional, not assumed.** Desired change #5 is gated behind F10's measurement because herdr already dedupes concurrent identical reads (in-flight memo, WL-0MV5CBQ6L005SPAG) and serves default-view reads in-process via `@worklog/shared` (WL-0MV6C6SLB005HX7B). The expected remaining gap is per-spawn boot cost.
- **D5 — `--version` uses the generated `src/version.ts`.** `getVersion()` currently lives in the 73 MB `cli-utils` graph; the fast path reads `WORKLOG_VERSION` directly so `wl --version` can exit at bare-node cost.
- **D6 — No daemon, no sync/JSONL changes** (intake Q1-A): the fast path changes only *when* modules load, never what is cached or how sync works.

### Appendix: planning-stage questions and decisions

Intake already recorded Q1 (stateless one-shot CLI, lazy imports, cache hygiene) and Q2 (CPU-second measurement, under 60 MB RSS, no correctness regression). The plan stage asked no new questions: the intake brief's measurements, desired-change list and answered decisions left no ambiguous choice that would change the decomposition. D1–D6 are recorded as assumptions for audit rather than as invented requirements.

- **OPEN QUESTION (for producer, non-blocking):** if F7 cannot reach 60 MB peak RSS (bare node is already 58 MB), should AC1's RSS limit become "within 3 MB of bare node", or should the fast path be allowed further Node startup work (e.g. a compile cache or snapshot)? F7 raises this with measured evidence rather than silently relaxing the AC.

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-19 — plan skill: decomposed into 11 child items (F1–F11) in test-first dependency order; created all children at `stage=intake_complete`; wired 15 dependency edges; recorded decisions D1–D6; effort/risk re-estimated from the child WBS.

# F1 — Spawn instrumentation: per-process CPU time and peak RSS

Extends the env-gated spawn instrumentation (WL-0MSGAEC5N006W5QA) so each `wl` process records its own CPU time and peak RSS. This is the measurement lever for parent AC2 (CPU-seconds per refresh cycle) and for the RSS half of parent AC1.

## Target outcome

`WL_SPAWN_COUNT_FILE` records gain `cpuMs` (user+system from `process.resourceUsage()`) and `maxRssKb`, so a coordinator can total CPU-seconds per refresh cycle and read per-process peak memory without an external sampler.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `SpawnRecord` carries `cpuMs` and `maxRssKb`; `recordSpawn()` appends `<kind>	<ts>	<pid>	<cpuMs>	<maxRssKb>`.
- Back-compat: 3-field legacy lines still parse, with CPU/RSS reported as `null` (not 0, so aggregation cannot silently under-report).
- `summariseSpawnRecords(file)` returns total records, per-kind counts, total CPU-seconds and max RSS over the file; covered by unit tests.
- Instrumentation stays best-effort: no throw and no behaviour change when the env vars are unset or the file is unwritable.
- `WL_SPAWN_COUNT=1` (stderr path) also reports CPU/RSS.
- `tests/cli/read-cache-spawn-reduction.test.ts` passes unchanged (kind counts unaffected).

## Minimal Implementation

1. Capture `process.resourceUsage()` at record time (`userCPUTime`/`systemCPUTime` are microseconds, `maxRSS` is KiB) and write the extended line.
2. Tolerate both line shapes in `readSpawnRecords()`.
3. Add the aggregation helper plus unit tests.

**Key Files:**
- `src/spawn-counter.ts`
- `tests/spawn-counter.test.ts`
- `tests/cli/read-cache-spawn-reduction.test.ts`

## Deliverables

- Extended instrumentation, aggregation helper and unit tests.
- A baseline comment on the parent recording CPU-seconds and p95 wall/RSS for `wl next --json`, `wl list --json`, `wl status`, `wl sync --if-idle` and `wl --version`.

# F2 — Startup import-budget harness (ratchet) and baseline capture

Builds the verification harness for parent AC1 without breaking the green tree: a checked-in budget/ratchet that records the current fast-path import graph and measured cost, which later items tighten. Also captures the pre-change baseline.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `bench/startup-import-budget.json` records (a) the set of modules statically reachable from `src/cli.ts`, (b) measured p95 wall time and peak RSS baselines for warm `wl next --json`, `wl list --status open --json` and `wl --version`, and (c) the parent AC1 target values (p95 <= 0.5 s, peak RSS <= 60 MB).
- **Ratchet test (always on, under one second):** walking static imports from `src/cli.ts` transitively, the test fails when a module is added to the graph. Removing modules is allowed and must be accompanied by a deliberate budget-file update, so every improvement is locked in and no regression slips through.
- **Regression test in the default suite:** measured p95 wall time stays within the recorded budget plus documented headroom; measurement is CPU-time based (`process.resourceUsage` via F1 spawn records) so a loaded shared host does not produce false failures, and the AC1 target is asserted once F4/F7 record it as the budget.
- **Reference-host report:** a benchmark script emits `--json` (p95 wall, peak RSS, CPU time, bare-node floor) for quoting in work-item comments; the exact command is documented so it can be re-run after F7.
- The harness works for both `src/` (tsx) and `dist/` (built) invocation, because `/usr/local/bin/wl` runs `dist/cli.js`, and for a served cache hit.
- Covers parent AC1's import budget: cache-hit reads and `--version` must not load command modules, the DB runtime, or plugins; the recorded budget tracks the reference-host p95 wall time <= 0.5 s and peak RSS <= 60 MB for warm `wl next --json` / `wl list --status open --json` cache hits.

## Minimal Implementation

1. `tests/cli/startup-import-budget.test.ts`: transitive static-import walk of `src/cli.ts` compared with the budget file, plus the timing regression assertion against the recorded budget.
2. `bench/wl-startup-perf.ts`: repeated warm runs (>= 10), p95 wall time, CPU time and RSS from F1 spawn records, bare-node floor reference, `--json` output.
3. `npm run benchmark:wl-startup` script entry.
4. Baseline comment on the parent with the measured numbers.

**Key Files:**
- `tests/cli/startup-import-budget.test.ts`
- `bench/startup-import-budget.json`
- `bench/wl-startup-perf.ts`
- `src/cli.ts`
- `package.json`

## Dependencies

- F1 (spawn records carry CPU time and RSS).

# F8 — Tests: cache state pruning, bounds and atomicity

Test-first coverage for parent AC3 (bounded, prunable `~/.cache/wl/state/`) and for the freshness invariants pruning must not break (parent AC4). Today `state/<sha256(dir)>.json` is one file per worklog dir ever seen (216,228 files, about 890 MB on the reference host) with no pruning path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Pruning tests cover: counters older than the TTL are removed; file count is capped at a configured bound (LRU by mtime) after a run; fresh and recently written counters are never removed.
- Atomicity/concurrency: pruning tolerates concurrent `bumpStateCounter` writers; a concurrent-writer test (pattern from `tests/read-cache-concurrent-child.ts`) asserts counter monotonicity and that a prune cannot reset a live counter.
- Freshness invariants unchanged: `tests/read-cache.test.ts`, `tests/read-cache-cli.test.ts` and `tests/cli/read-cache-e2e.test.ts` pass unchanged (write-to-read freshness, arg-variant separation, WAL-aware invalidation, byte-identical JSON).
- Bounded-state test: after 2x the bound of synthetic worklog dirs, `state/` holds no more than the bound and the cache still serves correct hits for surviving dirs.
- `wl doctor cache` behaviour is covered by CLI tests (exit code, `--json` shape, dry-run versus prune).
- Covers parent AC4: no correctness regression — write-to-read freshness, arg-variant separation, WAL-aware invalidation, concurrent readers and writers, and byte-identical JSON for identical (dir, argv, version); the existing read-cache, e2e and spawn-reduction suites pass unchanged.


**Key Files:**
- `tests/read-cache.test.ts`
- `tests/read-cache-cli.test.ts`
- `tests/read-cache-concurrent-child.ts`
- `tests/cli/read-cache-e2e.test.ts`
- `tests/cli/doctor-cache.test.ts`

## Dependencies

- None (can start immediately after F2's baseline capture).

# F4 — Split the CLI entry: thin fast path, dynamically imported heavy graph

Implements desired change #1: `src/cli.ts` becomes a thin bootstrap (argv scan, read-cache fast path, `--version`) that dynamically imports the current heavy graph (`src/cli-main.ts`) only when a cache hit did not serve the invocation. This is the largest single lever for parent AC1.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `src/cli.ts` statically imports only the fast-path allowlist; `commander`, command modules, `plugin-loader`, `cli-utils`, `lib/runtime` and `better-sqlite3` load only through dynamic `import()` inside `cli-main.ts`.
- The F2 budget file is tightened in the same change: the recorded fast-path graph becomes the allowlist, so a future eager import fails the ratchet test.
- A served cache hit exits before any heavy module loads; `wl --version` prints the version from `src/version.ts` and exits without heavy imports.
- Every command behaves identically: full suite green, including `tests/cli/read-cache-e2e.test.ts` and `tests/cli/read-cache-spawn-reduction.test.ts` unchanged (parent AC4).

# F9 — Bound and prune the cache state directory via `wl doctor cache`

Implements desired change #4 and parent AC3: make the per-worklog-dir state counters a bounded, prunable on-disk store with a documented maintenance path, without touching freshness semantics.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Opportunistic pruning on cache writes keeps `state/` at or under a configured bound (default file count around 1,000 plus a TTL for untouched counters, aligned with the existing entry TTL/LRU). # Herdr: coalesce the per-refresh `wl` spawns into one consolidated read

## Problem statement

A Herdr default-view refresh runs **five separate `wl` subprocesses per pane per tick**: the four mandatory `wl list` subsets plus the `wl next` browse feed (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`). Per-spawn Node bootstrap now dominates the cost (~66 % of the remaining 0.70 CPU-s/spawn is the bare-node floor), so F10 capped the achievable reduction at ~65 % with five spawns and missed the 60 % target (47.6 % achieved). The remaining lever is **fewer spawns**: one consolidated read per refresh tick.

## Users

- **Herdr pane operator** (producer/agent running several Herdr panes on one worklog): wants a responsive worklist without each pane burning CPU on five `wl` boots per tick.
- **Herdr plugin maintainer**: wants one simple, cacheable read seam instead of five coordinated queries with an in-flight memo.
- **wl CLI maintainer**: wants the consolidated command to reuse the existing DB-query and read-cache machinery, not fork it.

### Example user stories

- As a Herdr pane operator, when 4–5 panes refresh every 30 s against one shared worklog, total CPU consumption should drop to **≤ 0.4× the pre-F4 baseline** so the host stays responsive.
- As a Herdr plugin maintainer, I want `fetcher.ts` to issue **one `wl` read per refresh tick** (one DB open, one cache entry), with the displayed items unchanged.
- As an agent relying on the worklist, I want the **mandatory guarantees** (critical items, blocked items and the review queue always shown) preserved by tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A single `wl` invocation returns every subset the worklist needs — critical, in_review review queue, in-progress roots, blocked roots and the browse feed — as a **dedicated `wl worklist --json` command** (preferred) or an equivalent `--worklist-bundle` mode, sharing **one DB open and one read-cache entry**.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` issues that single read per default-view refresh tick; the mandatory-subset guarantees (critical always shown, blocked always shown, review queue always shown) are preserved by tests.
- Measured with `bench/herdr-refresh-cycle.ts` (F10): total CPU-seconds per 30 s cycle with 4 panes drops to **≤ 0.4× the pre-F4 baseline (≤ 63.8 CPU-s)**, ideally ~5× fewer spawns.
- Cache correctness unchanged: identical JSON for identical DB state, write invalidation still bumps the state counter, and worktree / `--worklog-dir` behaviour is unchanged.
- Herdr refresh output is unchanged for the same DB state (existing fetcher tests + the spawn-reduction simulation pass).
- **Testing/validation:** new tests cover the consolidated command's response shape, read-cache hit and write-invalidation, the fetcher's single-spawn path, mandatory-subset guarantees and output parity with the per-subset path.
- **Documentation:** all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries (notably `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md`).
- **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Pure read:** the bundle must not write. `wl next`'s auto re-sort is a write byproduct; the bundle must use `--no-re-sort`-style selection (or reuse the selection logic without the write) so the result is deterministically cacheable.
- **Cache reuse:** register the new invocation with the existing read-cache (`src/read-cache-cli.ts`), keyed by `(worklog-dir, argv)` and fingerprinted by the monotonic state counter; a mid-action write must not cache an unrepresentative payload.
- **Fail-open fallback:** if the consolidated read is unavailable or fails (older `wl`, malformed payload), the fetcher falls back to today's per-subset spawn path with unchanged behaviour.
- **No output change:** the consolidated response must feed the same `extractItems` → `selectWorkItems` → `regroupWorkItems` pipeline so ordering, grouping and audit enrichment are identical.
- **Bounded payload:** the browse feed stays limited by the caller's count; subsets are returned with the same filters (`--root-only` where applicable) so payload growth is bounded and no item duplication is unbounded.
- `--worklog-dir` (module override and per-call) and managed-worktree resolution semantics are unchanged.
- TypeScript/Node stack; match existing style; no new runtime dependency unless unavoidable.

## Existing state

- **fetcher.ts** — `fetchMandatorySubsets()` spawns four `wl list` queries in parallel (critical, review queue, in-progress roots, blocked roots); `fetchNextItems()` spawns `wl next` and calls `fetchMandatorySubsets()`, giving five spawns per default-view refresh. An in-flight fetch memo deduplicates *identical* concurrent reads (which collapses the review-queue state query into the review subset), and `fetchChildrenForItems` / `fetchActionableCount` already read in-process from SQLite via one refresh-scoped connection.
- **Read cache** — `src/read-cache.ts` / `src/read-cache-cli.ts` serve `list`, `next`, `show`, `search` and `status` JSON from a shared on-disk cache keyed by `(worklog-dir, argv)`, fingerprinted by a monotonic per-worklog-dir write counter; writes bump the counter and drop entries. `src/cli.ts` performs the lookup before loading the heavy command graph.
- **CLI commands** — `src/commands/*.ts` register subcommands through `src/plugin-types.ts` / `src/command-registry.ts`; `next.ts` owns the auto re-sort and the selection semantics; `list.ts` owns the filtered list queries.
- **Measurement** — `bench/herdr-refresh-cycle.ts` (F10, 4 panes × 30 s × 5 s tick, sums per-process CPU from spawn records) and `bench/herdr-refresh-perf.ts` (spawn-count/latency per refresh).
- **F10 numbers** — pre-F4 baseline 159.44 CPU-s/cycle, after F4–F7 83.58 CPU-s/cycle (47.6 % reduction), target 63.78; per-spawn 1.329 → 0.697 CPU-s against a ~0.46 CPU-s bare-node floor.

## Desired change

1. Add a consolidated worklist read to the `wl` CLI — preferably a new `wl worklist --json` command — that opens the database **once** and returns the critical, review-queue, in-progress-root, blocked-root and browse-feed subsets in one payload, built from the same query/selection code the individual commands use.
2. Make it a cacheable read invocation (one cache entry, same state-counter fingerprint and write invalidation), so repeat refreshes across panes hit the cache as a single entry.
3. Change `fetcher.ts` so the default-view refresh drives that one read (with the review-queue state and browse feed derived from it) and retains the existing per-subset path as a fail-open fallback.
4. Add coverage: command unit/integration tests, cache hit/invalidation tests, fetcher single-spawn and mandatory-guarantee tests, and an output-parity test against the per-subset path; update the spawn-reduction simulation and the benchmark expectations.
5. Update `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` and any CLI reference docs/comments.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/commands/worklist.ts` — **new** consolidated read command (or a `--worklist-bundle` mode added to `src/commands/list.ts`)
- `src/command-registry.ts` — register the new command
- `src/read-cache-cli.ts` — add the invocation to `READ_CACHE_COMMANDS` / cacheability checks
- `src/cli.ts` — cache lookup path (expected unchanged; verify the new command is served before the heavy graph)
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — single consolidated read, review-state/browse derivation, fail-open fallback
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `doRefresh` wiring so the bundle replaces the per-subset fan-out
- `tests/cli/read-cache-spawn-reduction.test.ts` — spawn-reduction simulation uses the consolidated invocation
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher-*.test.ts` — mandatory-subset, review-queue and output-parity coverage
- `bench/herdr-refresh-cycle.ts` — measurement harness (expects the consolidated query)
- `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` — cold-refresh cost section updated

## Related work

- **F10 — WL-0MVFRRS2I000G93J** (completed): measured the <= 60 % shortfall and filed this item with the spawn-count lever. This item is the follow-up implementation of that lever.
- **WL-0MVFNMSRW002FI6B** (completed, outbound dependency): spawn-load epic — transient `wl` process CPU usage.
- **WL-0MV5CBQ6L005SPAG** (completed): cut cold refresh cost — in-process SQLite reads, in-flight fetch memo, batched expanded children. The consolidated read builds on this.
- **WL-0MV6C6SLB005HX7B** (completed): one shared in-process connection per refresh — related "one open per refresh" precedent.
- **WL-0MV02VA29009WBEN** (completed): make Herdr refresh snappy after agent updates — parent of the earlier performance work.
- **Docs:** `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md`, `docs/dev/wl-spawn-baseline-2026-10-19.md`, `docs/benchmarks/wal-read-latency-benchmark.md`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Cache staleness (risk, high):** a single cache entry must never serve stale data across a write. Mitigation: reuse the counter fingerprint, cache only when the counter is unchanged since lookup, and add an explicit write-invalidation test.
- **Re-sort write byproduct (risk, medium):** today's `wl next` runs an auto re-sort (a DB write) on some invocations. The bundle must be a pure read; assumption: `--no-re-sort` selection produces the same displayed order for a stable DB. Verify with an output-parity test; if ordering genuinely differs, resolve the re-sort as a separate, explicitly-documented concern rather than making the bundle a write.
- **Mandatory-subset regression (risk, high):** a bundle that silently drops a subset breaks the always-shown guarantees. Mitigation: tests assert each mandatory subset is present regardless of the browse window.
- **Backwards compatibility (risk, low):** an older `wl` without the new command. Mitigation: fall back to the per-subset spawn path (fail-open).
- **Cross-subset consistency (risk, medium):** the five subsets are read in one process but through separate queries; a write landing mid-bundle could make the subsets disagree. Mitigation: serve all subsets from one DB connection inside a read transaction (or the same store snapshot) so the payload reflects one stable state; at minimum, match today's eventual-consistency behaviour and document it.
- **Payload size (risk, low):** five subsets in one payload. Mitigation: keep the browse feed count-bounded and reuse the existing dedupe/merge pipeline.
- **Scope creep (risk, medium):** further per-spawn startup optimisation (F4–F7) is out of scope. Record additional opportunities as linked work items, not scope.
- **Assumption:** `wl` and the Herdr plugin ship together from this repository, so the fetcher may rely on the new command in the same release; the fallback remains for robustness.

## Verification plan


# Herdr downtime dispatch: use the proxy's local_idle_seconds as the idle-age signal

## Problem statement

The llama-proxy now publishes an authoritative local idle age
(`local_idle_seconds`, plus `local_last_activity_at` and
`local_last_activity_source`), but herdr measures idle duration itself from
its own polls. If the GPU has already been idle for hours when herdr starts
polling (plugin restart, pane restart, resumed session), herdr still waits a
full `downtimeIdleThresholdMs` before dispatching; conversely its sampled
tracker can be fooled by gaps in polling. Both outcomes leave the local model
idle when it could be working.

## Users

- **Operator / producer:** wants downtime dispatch to start as soon as the
  local GPU has genuinely been idle long enough, including immediately after
  a herdr restart.
- **Downtime dispatcher (herdr plugin):** wants the proxy's authoritative
  idle age instead of inferring it from poll cadence.

Example stories:

- As the operator, after restarting herdr while the GPU has been idle for two
  hours, I want the next downtime pane dispatched on the first poll rather
  than after another threshold wait.
- As the dispatcher, when the proxy reports `local_idle_seconds` below the
  threshold, I should not dispatch even if my local tracker has an older idle
  run (the proxy is authoritative).

## Evidence / existing state (llm-manager)

Upstream capability is **already implemented and deployed** on llm-manager
`dev` (commit `05986c1b`, `LP-0MVGD9Z8Z0055Y5J`). `GET /llama/local/status`
now serves:

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `local_idle_seconds` | `float \| null` | Monotonic idle age of the local backend; updated on dispatch start, on every forwarded SSE chunk, and on request finish. Baseline is proxy process start, so a freshly restarted proxy reports its true idle age rather than "unknown". |
| `local_last_activity_at` | ISO string \| null | Wall-clock timestamp of the last local activity (operator-facing). |
| `local_last_activity_source` | string \| null | What last touched the backend (`dispatch` / `chunk` / `finish` / startup …). |

The same upstream change also added idle-aware local admission on the proxy
(`local_idle_admit_enabled`, default off), which reads exactly this signal.

Relevant existing herdr behaviour (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`):

- `createIdleTracker()` records idle runs from the worker's own poll results;
  `downtimeIdleThresholdMs` is the continuous-idle threshold.
- Per-slot mode tracks the same N slots continuously free
  (`perSlotTracker.thresholdMetCount`).
- `globalIdleChecks()` requires `local_active_query === false` (all-slots-free
  mode); the spare-capacity path relaxes it.
- `LlamaStatus` does **not** parse `local_idle_seconds`.

Contract source: llm-manager `proxy/docs/routing.md` § "Idle-aware local
admission" (idle signal description) and
`proxy/docs/per-slot-status-verification.md`.

## Desired change

1. Extend `LlamaStatus` / `parseLlamaStatus` with `local_idle_seconds`,
   `local_last_activity_at` and `local_last_activity_source` (all optional;
   malformed values degrade to `undefined`, never throw).
2. When `local_idle_seconds` is present and finite, use it as the
   **authoritative** idle-age signal for threshold qualification:
   - `idle_seconds >= thresholdSeconds` → the idle threshold is already met
     on this poll (no need to wait for the local tracker to accumulate).
   - `idle_seconds < thresholdSeconds` → not yet qualified; do **not** admit
     on the strength of an older local tracker run (the proxy is
     authoritative).
   - absent / non-finite → fall back to today's local tracker behaviour
     exactly (pre-feature proxy).
3. Keep the immediate busy reset: a poll that shows activity
   (`is_processing`, a live lease, any contention/gate waiter) still resets
   the idle run regardless of the reported idle age.
4. Use `local_last_activity_source` in the decision log (and optionally the
   header) to explain *why* the backend is considered busy/idle (e.g.
   `chunk`, `dispatch`, `finish`) — this is operator-facing evidence, not a
   gate.
5. Do not weaken the per-slot contract: `local_idle_seconds` is a global
   signal; it may only *satisfy* the per-slot continuous-free requirement
   when the same poll also provides usable per-slot detail and no slot is
   processing/owned. If per-slot detail is absent/empty/stale, the existing
   `slots-unavailable` fail-closed path still applies.
6. Preserve `requiredFreeSlots` semantics: the idle-age signal qualifies the
   *duration*, not the *capacity*; the free-slot budget is unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `parseLlamaStatus` reads `local_idle_seconds`,
  `local_last_activity_at` and `local_last_activity_source`; absent fields
  preserve today's behaviour, and malformed values degrade to `undefined`
  without throwing (tests).
- [ ] With `local_idle_seconds >= thresholdSeconds` reported on the first
  poll (fresh worker, usable per-slot detail, no activity), the worker
  dispatches without waiting for the local tracker to accumulate the
  threshold (test).
- [ ] With `local_idle_seconds < thresholdSeconds`, the worker does **not**
  dispatch even when its local tracker already has an older idle run (test).
- [ ] A poll reporting activity (per-slot `is_processing`, live lease, or a
  contention/gate waiter) resets the idle run regardless of a large
  `local_idle_seconds` (test).
- [ ] `local_idle_seconds` absent (pre-feature proxy) restores exactly
  today's local-tracker behaviour (regression test).
- [ ] `slots_stale: true`, `slots: []` or unusable per-slot detail still
  yields `slots-unavailable` even when `local_idle_seconds` is large (test —
  the global signal must not bypass the per-slot fail-closed contract).
- [ ] The decision log records `local_idle_seconds` (and
  `local_last_activity_source` when present) so an operator can see why a
  dispatch was admitted or deferred (test asserts the logged fields).
- [ ] Tests are written red-first and cover every transition above using the
  existing fixtures (`downtime-worker.parse.test.ts`,
  `downtime-worker.idle.test.ts`, `downtime-worker.fixtures.ts`).
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
  code comments, `packages/herdr/README.md` (idle detection description and
  `downtimeIdleThresholdMs`) and `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (idle-age
  authority and fallback behaviour).
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Backward compatible:** absent idle fields must behave exactly as today.
- **Fail closed on ambiguity:** a non-finite/malformed idle age is ignored
  (fallback to the local tracker), never treated as "idle forever".
- **Global signal, local contract:** `local_idle_seconds` never bypasses the
  per-slot availability/fail-closed rules.
- **No new polling:** reuse the existing single-flight status poll.
- Keep the change surgical: prefill/concurrency pacing is the sibling item
  `WL-0MVHSZRZQ00482QX`; per-slot `lease_state`/`capacity_hint` availability
  is `WL-0MVHSZQVX0000T6P`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `LlamaStatus`,
  `parseLlamaStatus`, `createIdleTracker` / tick idle qualification,
  per-slot tick path, decision-log builder, `decisionHeaderToken` if a new
  reason is introduced.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.parse.test.ts` — new fields,
  malformed/absent cases.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.idle.test.ts` — threshold
  qualification, busy reset, stale/unusable interplay.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` — end-to-end tick and
  decision-log assertions.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.fixtures.ts` — idle-signal fixtures.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — idle detection contract and threshold.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — idle-age authority.

## Related work

**Upstream (llm-manager)**

- `LP-0MVGD9Z8Z0055Y5J` — Idle-aware local admission for large/cold prompts —
  completed (`05986c1b`); publishes `local_idle_seconds` and the activity
  source.
- `LP-0MVGDUVGE0024YAI` — truthful capacity payload (`capacity_hint`,
  `lease_state`); the availability sibling.
- `LP-0MVGDUUV3001XFRJ` — prefill serialisation; the pacing sibling.
- `LP-0MVECWYWK000U3E1` — stale log-derived slot-progress expiry; keeps the
  per-slot `n_decoded` signal honest (a related proxy-side fix).

**ContextHub**

- `WL-0MVHSZQVX0000T6P` — **blocks this item**: truthful per-slot capacity
  parsing/gating.
- `WL-0MVHSZRZQ00482QX` — sibling: prefill-serialisation pacing.
- `WL-0MSP28LSY007NDYX` / `WL-0MT3D585I0070FF0` — per-slot idle tracking and
  the relaxed idle gate (the behaviour this item qualifies).
- `WL-0MSL2ZQIF006QB4Q` — `local_active_query` as the local busy signal
  (precedent for preferring a proxy-authoritative signal).
- `WL-0MUXVPXAZ005RESW` — fail-closed per-slot contract.

## Risks / assumptions

- **Risk — clock/baseline semantics:** `local_idle_seconds` is monotonic and
  proxy-process-relative; a proxy restart resets it to a small value even if
  the GPU was idle before. The local tracker remains a valid fallback, so the
  worker may still wait a threshold after a proxy restart — acceptable and
  documented.
- **Risk — bypassing per-slot continuous-free semantics:** mitigated by
  keeping the per-slot fail-closed preconditions and only using the global
  age as a *duration* qualification.
- **Assumption** — `local_idle_seconds` reflects all local activity
  (dispatch start, chunks, finish), so "idle ≥ threshold" implies every slot
  has been idle that long.
- **Assumption** — `downtimeIdleThresholdMs` remains the user-facing
  threshold; no new setting is needed.
- **Scope-creep risk:** do not expand into proxy admission changes
  (`local_idle_admit_enabled`) — that is upstream and off by default.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interview questions were required: the upstream implementation and its
published contract fully determine this brief. Evidence reviewed:

- llm-manager `dev` commit `05986c1b`, `proxy/docs/routing.md`
  § "Idle-aware local admission", `proxy/proxy/local_activity.py`.
- llm-manager `LP-0MVGD9Z8Z0055Y5J` description and acceptance criteria.
- llm-manager `proxy/proxy/handlers.py` `get_llama_local_status()` idle
  fields.
- ContextHub `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` (`createIdleTracker`,
  `evaluateIdle`, per-slot tick), `packages/herdr/README.md`,
  `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`.
- Worklog searches: `local_idle_seconds`, `idle`, `slot` — no existing
  ContextHub idle-age consumer item found (duplicate check performed).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MVHSZQVX0000T6P** – Herdr downtime dispatch: consume truthful per-slot capacity (lease_state / capacity_hint / prefill ETA) (in-progress)
- **WL-0MVHSZRZQ00482QX** – Herdr downtime dispatch: pace dispatch to local prefill serialisation (blocked)
- **WL-0MUV0VEFW007ZBB7** – Raise default downtime idle threshold to 75s so active sessions reclaim freed slots before dispatch (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: 0muxvpxaz005resw, absent, acceptable, acceptance, active (+298 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: 0muxvpxaz005resw, absent, accumulate, active, activity (+285 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: absent, active, activity, added, age (+225 more)
